note.question: How should effects of incentive contracts in online labor platforms be estimated?
note.overview: The design of performance-based incentives—commonly used in online labor platforms—can be naturally posed as a moral hazard principal-agent problem. In this setting, a key input to the principal’s optimal contracting problem is the agent’s production function: the dependence of agent output on effort. Although agent production is classically assumed to be known to the principal, this is unlikely to be the case in practice.
